title: Elevator system requirements
idea: Scoping an elevator system means naming who presses buttons, what the controller must decide, the safety rule it never breaks, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Passengers call a car from a floor, then choose a destination inside.
The controller picks which car answers each hall call, then moves it.
The safety rule: a car never moves while its doors are open.
Assume one building, about 16 floors and 3 cars; label them as assumptions.

nodes.label: Passenger
nodes.sub: on a floor or in a car

edges.caption: A passenger on a floor presses UP or DOWN. That is a hall call: a floor and a direction.
The controller receives the hall call and decides which car answers it.
Inside the car, the passenger presses a floor number. That is a car call for that one car.
A car call needs no choice of car. It becomes a stop on the car the rider is in.
The chosen car adds the stop, travels, and opens its doors only when stopped.
An operator takes a car out of service for repair. Its open calls must go to another car.
Destination keypads and fire service mode wait for a later version. Say so out loud.

code.title: Use cases as an enum
code.caption: The scope written as code: each use case has one actor, and v1 is an explicit set.

walk.text: v1 is a named set. Anything missing from it is out of scope by default.
Print every use case with its actor and an IN or OUT tag.
Scale is stated as an assumption, not as a measured fact.
Three actors: the passenger, the operator, and the system itself.
Six use cases cover calling, riding, dispatching and maintenance.
Destination keypads and fire mode are listed, so the cut is visible.

pitfalls: Do not design scheduling before agreeing what hall calls and car calls are.
State floors, cars and peak traffic as assumptions, never as measured facts.
Leaving out the operator hides maintenance and failover until too late.

quiz.q: Three people on floor 5 press UP within two seconds. What should v1 do?
options: Dispatch three cars, one per press
Keep one open UP call for floor 5
Reject the second and third press
Queue three calls and serve them in order
quiz.why: A hall call means someone on this floor wants to go up. Extra presses add nothing, so the system keeps one open call per floor and button.

takeaway: Name actors, hall and car calls, and the doors-closed rule first.

starters: What is the difference between a hall call and a car call?
Should fire service mode ever be in v1 scope?
Which scale assumptions should I state for an elevator interview?
